newsitem.title: USA: Dow powers past 8,000 record, techs keep surging.
newsitem.headline: Dow powers past 8,000 record, techs keep surging.

text.p: The Dow industrials made a mighty stride past the record 8,000 level by midday on Wednesday, while technology stocks roared to fresh highs.

The Dow Jones Industrial average climbed despite steep losses in component Eastman Kodak Co, which posted below-forecast quarterly results. After briefly crossing 8,000 several times in the morning, it was up 42 points at 8019.
The Dow then extended gains, rising over 50 points and prompting the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading.
A soaring technology sector gave power to the broader equities markets, as the Nasdaq composite added around 27 points, or 1.74 percent, to 1569.
Solid quarterly earnings reports, including better-than-expected results from giant chipmaker Intel Corp, and lower bond yields drove share prices to fresh highs, analysts said.

"Nasdaq stocks are leading the way, earnings have been relatively good apart from Kodak, there's momentum and interest rates keep coming down," Warren Epstein, director of trading at Richard Rosenblatt, said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was up 27/32, piercing critical resistance to yield 6.48 percent.
It took off after a 0.1 percent gain in the June consumer price index, which pointed to tame inflation, analysts said.
"The data this morning was incredibly favorable," Chris Dickerson, an analyst at Global Market Strategists, said. "Sightings of inflation are as rare as sightings of unicorns."
The Standard & Poor's 500 index gained around eight points to 934, and the Russell 2000 index of small capitalization shares tacked on roughly three points to 409.
"There's strength across the board," said John Cleland, chief investment strategst at Security Benefit Group of Cos. "The techonology stocks are just exploding here."

The technology sector adopted a euphoric tone after Intel, the world's largest producer of microprocessors, reported second quarter earnings of $0.92 per share compared with $0.59 per share in the year-ago quarter and the First Call consensus estimate of $0.90 per share.

Intel surged 4-29/32 to 85-13/16, while Microsoft Corp, due to report earnings tomorrow, gained 7-27/32 to 146-5/16. Compaq Computer Corp rose 2-1/8 to 129-1/2 and Sun Microsystems Inc rose 2-9/16 to 44-1/8.

"In this market, people are afraid to sell, afraid of being left behind," Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist & director, asset allocation at PanAgora Asset Management Inc. "But the techs are still reasonably valued because their growth rates are high."
Tech stocks looked past declines in Kodak, which posted second quarter earnings of $1.12 per share.
The First Call consensus estimate was for $1.39 per share. Kodak's stock dropped 7-7/8 to 69.
"With Eastman Kodak down around 8-1/2, that's the equivalent of about 32 points in the Dow," Epstein said.
Drug shares were softer after Pfizer Corp reported slightly lower-than-expected earnings of $0.35 per share.
Pfizer's stock shed 2-1/4 to 59-7/16 and Dow component Merck & Co lost 1-9/16 to 99.
ITT Corp stock gained 5-1/8 to 67-3/4. The company said it would split into three separate companies to fend off a takeover bid from rival Hilton Hotels Corp.
((Wall Street desk 212-859=1730))
